clue.text: New plan to re-use drink

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
a chart is a plan or map
taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: A scheme to recycle something to drink, perhaps a bottle of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New plan' looks like an anagram signal, but GREEN and CHART are straight synonyms; GREEN CHARTREUSE is the herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks.
explanation.definitionFit: Green Chartreuse is a strong French herbal liqueur, so it is one particular kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Old Observer man has friend round for music

indicators.note: one word has the other, holding it inside, while 'round' places it around
round says the friend is placed around the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a pal is a friend
David Astor was the long-serving editor and owner of The Observer newspaper

explanation.surface: A former newspaper man brings a friend round to listen to some music.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, edited for decades by David Astor of the Astor family.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral is a piece of music evoking rural, country life, such as Beethoven's Pastoral Symphony.

clue.text: Some peculiar denizens of the forest

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run lying inside them

parts.note: the run straddles the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Odd creatures that live in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of 'peculiar' and the start of 'denizens'. Arden is the forest of As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Arden is a real woodland in Warwickshire and the setting of Shakespeare's comedy As You Like It.

clue.text: Clarify an occurrence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to make plain by citing an example
second meaning: a noun, a single case of something happening

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is the less familiar one: to instance something is to give it as an example, which makes a point clearer.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to cite as an example to explain; as a noun it is one case or occurrence of something.

clue.text: Programme already seen about fuel

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning, about
peat is dug and burned as fuel

explanation.surface: A rerun of a TV show about energy sources.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat is a broadcast shown again, so viewers have watched it on an earlier occasion.

clue.text: Declaration of intention to clear ring

parts.note: manifest means clear or obvious
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone announces a plan to clear out a criminal ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a public statement of the policies and aims a party or person plans to pursue.

clue.text: Not watching at start?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: with the television set switched off
second meaning: to begin a journey

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful reading: if your TV set is off, you are not watching it. The question mark flags this whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is a phrasal verb for beginning a trip or departing, so it can replace start.

clue.text: Elucidate muddle in the marking scale

indicators.note: to muddle the following words is to jumble them into disorder

parts.note: all fifteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A teacher explains a confusion in how exam grades are awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to explain or throw light on something, which the phrase expresses in plain everyday words.

clue.text: Make fresh disposition in back rank

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row or line, as a rank is

explanation.surface: An officer reorganises the soldiers standing in the back line.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposition here means arrangement or placement, so making a new one means ordering things differently.

clue.text: Sphere of action where a soldier faces an about turn

parts.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, so a soldier

indicators.note: an about turn is a soldier's drill order to face the opposite way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A parade ground where a soldier is ordered to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a corps of the British Army, abbreviated RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is figuratively a field or scene of activity, like the political arena.

clue.text: Ask to tear net in pieces

indicators.note: broken into pieces, the words are reassembled in a fresh order

parts.note: both words are used whole

explanation.surface: A request for someone to rip up a net into bits.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly or plead, a stronger form of making a request.

clue.text: Does pie-cooking become an event?

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: both words are used whole

explanation.surface: Is baking a pie really such a big occasion?
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single incident or happening, one distinct event in a series.

clue.text: Centre returns some of the rockets

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read from right to left
only a portion of the following words' letters is taken

parts.note: a run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A control centre sends back some of its launched rockets.
explanation.definitionFit: The core is the central or innermost part of something, as of an apple.

clue.text: He left town confused by a fraction

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their order

parts.note: all three words are used whole

explanation.surface: A man quits town, baffled by some arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: One twelfth is a specific fraction, a single part of a whole divided into twelve.

clue.text: Begins to sort out inside office workers

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: staff are the people employed in an office

indicators.note: sort out suggests rearranging, and out signals the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: A manager starts organising what the office employees are doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort out' reads as one phrase, but 'sort' is the fodder and 'out' the jumble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Starts off is a phrasal verb meaning commences, the same as begins in the third person singular.

clue.text: A rewritten letter to a French girl

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something rewritten is set out again in a different form

parts.note: taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone redrafts a letter addressed to a young Frenchwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Arlette is a French female given name, so it fits a girl from France.

clue.text: Touch bird gently by design

parts.note: to pat is to touch lightly, as the word gently further on hints
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone strokes a bird softly, on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By design' means deliberately, but here 'design' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a decorative design, such as a repeated motif on fabric or wallpaper.

clue.text: Urge fellow to become a reporter

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Encouraging a chap to take up journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressman is a journalist, someone who works for the newspapers, collectively called the press.

clue.text: Broken toes boy keeps secret

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name

indicators.note: broken toes have been knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: A lad hides the fact that he has fractured his toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means known only to a small inner circle, so it is hidden or private knowledge.

clue.text: Writers torn asunder in old Egyptian city

indicators.note: in places the jumbled piece within the city

parts.note: Thebes was the ancient capital of Egypt

indicators.note: torn asunder means ripped apart, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: Authors being ripped apart in an ancient city of Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torn asunder' reads as one phrase, but 'torn' is the fodder and 'asunder' the jumble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne were the three novelist sisters, collectively known by their surname.

clue.text: Ale drunk by Edward in high spirits

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before being jumbled
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward has had some beer and is now very cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means joyful and exhilarated, which is what being in high spirits describes.

clue.text: One who puts on nothing in dust storm

indicators.note: a storm whirls things about, scattering the letters

parts.note: both words are used whole

explanation.surface: Someone caught naked in a dust storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist goes without clothing by choice, so dresses in nothing at all.

clue.text: He manages a stud

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person in charge of workers
second meaning: a raised knob or ornament on a surface

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone running a stud farm for horses, but stud here is a knob, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is an employer or manager, and also a round raised knob, like a stud on a shield.

clue.text: Way to get on in the theatre

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a step or phase on the way to making progress
second meaning: the acting profession as a whole

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests advice on succeeding as an actor; one meaning is a step in progress, the other the profession itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage is a step in progress, and the stage means the theatrical profession, as in going on the stage.

clue.text: Passed away inordinately pleased

indicators.note: read as in-ordinate, out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone died, and somebody else seems far too happy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed away' looks like dying, but it is time slipping by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has gone by or slipped away, the sense of passed away here.

clue.text: Writer who may look good on a horse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a member of a literary family of English authors

definitions.text: may look good on a horse
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rider with a fine seat in the saddle, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell Sitwell were English writers; split in two, the surname describes a good rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Sitwell was a celebrated English poet, and to sit well is to ride with good posture.

clue.text: Woman with a fine bundle

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A lady carrying a good-looking bundle of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle of things tied together, such as stalks of corn or papers.

clue.text: Girl has an insane view of utopia

indicators.note: an insane mind is disordered, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: all three words are used whole

explanation.surface: A young woman holds a crazy idea of a perfect society.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the paradise valley in James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, now a byword for an ideal place.
